claims.text: The feedstock is a FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloy with a particle-size range of 15–45 μm.
The 15–45 μm feedstock was previously used for HVAF-M3 deposition.
Setting the HVAF-i7 stand-off distance to approximately 300–350 mm will overcome the coating-thickness limitation.
A spray distance of 300–350 mm produced higher particle velocity in prior MCrAlY studies using the M3 system.
A spray distance of 300–350 mm produced higher deposition efficiency in prior MCrAlY studies using the M3 system.
Changing the stand-off distance to 300–350 mm will increase particle velocity relative to the default HVAF-i7 setting.
Higher particle velocity increases the in-flight kinetic energy of the particles.
Higher impact kinetic energy promotes a greater deposition rate.
Higher impact kinetic energy improves particle bonding efficiency.
Shortening the spray distance to 300–350 mm increases particle velocity at impact.
The resulting increase in deposition efficiency will overcome the coating-growth limitation.
The adjusted spray distance will preserve acceptable adhesion.
The adjusted spray distance will preserve low as-sprayed oxidation.
The adjusted process will produce a thicker bond coat than the default HVAF-i7 process using 15–45 μm feedstock.
The thicker coating will retain acceptable coating integrity and oxidation level.
The baseline HVAF-i7 process produced coatings of acceptable quality but inadequate thickness.
The intervention should remain effective for deposition in internal diameters as small as 120 mm.
The coating should retain integrity, adhesion, and oxidation resistance under high-temperature thermal-barrier service.
A lack of statistically significant thickness increase relative to the default-distance control would falsify the hypothesis.
Deterioration in coating integrity, adhesion, or oxidation resistance under the adjusted-distance condition would falsify the hypothesis.
